clue.text: Having more than enough of a corporation?

definitions.text: Having more than enough of a corporation?

parts.words: Having more than enough of a corporation?
parts.note: a 'corporation' is an old jocular word for a pot belly, so the phrase for being fed up is read literally as the amount that fills a paunch

explanation.surface: Someone is sick and tired of dealing with a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a business, but it is old slang for a large stomach, so having had too much of one is a stomach filled to capacity.
explanation.definitionFit: To have had one's fill of something, literally a full stomach, is the idiom for being thoroughly fed up.

clue.text: Trip to Danube beginning in Strasbourg is this

definitions.text: Trip to Danube beginning in Strasbourg is this
definitions.note: Strasbourg lies on the Rhine at France's eastern edge and the Danube rises further east in Germany, so the journey heads towards the sunrise

indicators.note: trip suggests the letters of to Danube stumble into a new order
beginning in picks the opening letter of Strasbourg

explanation.surface: A traveller describes the direction of a journey from Strasbourg to the Danube.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' is the anagram signal, not a journey: TO DANUBE plus the S from 'beginning in Strasbourg' are rearranged. Read whole, the clue says the source of the Danube lies east of Strasbourg.
explanation.definitionFit: Strasbourg sits on the Rhine, and the Danube rises further toward the sunrise in Germany's Black Forest, so the journey heads that way.

clue.text: Composer in catalogue heard

indicators.note: heard says the word for catalogue is spoken and we enter what it sounds like

parts.note: a catalogue is a list of items

explanation.surface: A composer's name turns up when someone hears a music catalogue read out.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz Liszt, the Hungarian pianist-composer, has a surname pronounced like the word for an itemised record.
explanation.definitionFit: Liszt was a nineteenth-century Hungarian pianist who wrote the Hungarian Rhapsodies, a famous example of a music writer.

clue.text: Northern sport and what one contestant may have done during it

definitions.meaning: a race on foot over the hills (fells) of northern England's Lake District and Pennines

definitions.text: what one contestant may have done during it
definitions.meaning: read as two words: a racer tumbled while on the move

explanation.walkthrough: Fells are the high moorland hills of northern England, hence 'Northern'; the second reading splits the phrase into a past-tense verb for falling plus 'running'.
explanation.definitionFit: The sport is hill racing over Cumbrian fells; the second sense is a runner taking a tumble mid-race.

clue.text: See straggler pull girl up

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' tells us to read the pull and the girl from bottom to top

parts.note: to drag something is to pull it
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: Someone is told to watch a slowcoach haul a young woman to her feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole run of pull and girl, giving LAG + GARD from DRAG + GAL; 'See' is just a link inviting us to look.
explanation.definitionFit: A straggler is one who falls behind the rest, the same as a dawdler or slowcoach.

clue.text: Actor's performing with me?

definitions.note: an actor speaking of a fellow principal who shares top billing in the same production

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters of Actor's go through their paces in a new order

explanation.surface: An actor wonders whether another player is on stage alongside them.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: an actor sharing the bill with the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow lead who shares billing in a film or play is a joint principal performer with the speaker.

clue.text: Trim, attractive young girl? That's out

indicators.note: out says the letters standing for 'that is' are removed from the word for the girl

parts.note: a cutie is an informal word for an attractive young woman
That's expands to 'that is', abbreviated i.e. (id est)

explanation.surface: A pretty young girl is told she's no longer in fashion, slim though she is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' must be read as 'that is', whose abbreviation IE is taken out of CUTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim hair or a hedge is to shorten it with scissors or shears.

clue.text: Putting awry, tiger seen in reserve

indicators.note: putting the letters awry means setting them askew, so the words tiger seen are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tiger is spotted in a game park, its pose looking off-kilter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a vast Tanzanian national park, a protected wildlife area of savanna.

clue.text: Gas man finally following a right turn

indicators.note: following places the letter from 'man' after the pieces built from a right turn

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in 'your go' in a game

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word man

explanation.surface: A gas fitter arrives at last after taking a right turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' is not a direction here but a turn in a game, GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is a noble element, an inert colourless constituent of air used in light bulbs.

clue.text: Express poll, support unchanged

indicators.note: to express is to squeeze out, and a poll is a head, so the head letter of the word for support is forced out

parts.note: a basis is a support or foundation

explanation.surface: A newspaper's opinion poll shows a party's backing holding steady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' wants to be the newspaper and 'poll' a survey; read instead as 'squeeze out the head', they remove the B from BASIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the existing condition, without alteration, as goods sold without warranty.

clue.text: Transference of cargo in less serious times?

parts.note: lighter means more frivolous, less weighty
an age is a period of time, as in 'the times we live in'

explanation.surface: Cargo handling is pictured as happening in a more frivolous era.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is the business of ferrying goods between ship and shore in flat-bottomed barges called lighters; the question mark flags the punning split.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighterage is the unloading of a ship's goods into barges, a form of cargo transfer in port.

clue.text: In passing round book, I rip answer out

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: out says the letter for answer is dropped from the word for rip

parts.note: to tear is to rip

explanation.surface: A reader furiously tears pages from a book in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: TEAR without its A gives TER; the definition is Latin, as in 'obiter dictum', a remark made by the way.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal word means incidentally, by the way, as in a judge's aside or obiter dictum.

clue.text: A liberal row about old and new combination

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal, a UK political party

indicators.note: about means the word for row goes round the letters for old and new

parts.note: a line is a row, as in a line of chairs

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician argues about combining the old with the new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' wants to be a quarrel, but here it is a line; 'about' wraps LINE round ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Something all-in-one combines several functions in a single unit, like a combined printer and scanner.

clue.text: What Churchill did around fashionable artist quarter?

definitions.text: What Churchill did around fashionable artist quarter?

indicators.note: around means the word for what Churchill did goes round the word for fashionable

parts.note: Churchill led Britain through the Second World War
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
a wing is a section or quarter of a building

explanation.surface: Churchill, a keen amateur painter, is pictured sketching near a trendy artists' district.
explanation.walkthrough: Churchill led Britain in wartime, and he was also a keen amateur painter, so the whole clue also describes his art. A Royal Academician is the stock crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Churchill was a keen amateur painter, and a sketch made of outlines is one kind of artwork he might have produced.

clue.text: Looking for teacher in place

parts.note: hunting means searching or looking for
a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: Someone is searching for a schoolteacher somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Huntingdon is a market town in Cambridgeshire, England; 'place' is a deliberately vague definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Huntingdon is a market town in Cambridgeshire, so it is a named location in England.

clue.text: Tycoon's capital behind housing firm: he'll look after it

indicators.note: capital means the opening, upper-case letter of the word Tycoon's
housing means the word for behind holds the word for firm inside it

parts.note: the rear is what is behind
sure means firm or steady, as in a sure footing

explanation.surface: A rich businessman's money sits behind a company, with someone appointed to guard it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money in this financial surface, but it means the capital letter of 'Tycoon's'; 'housing' wraps one piece round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer is the officer who manages and safeguards an organisation's funds, i.e. the money referred to.

clue.text: Advantage in golf club? No women!

indicators.note: No women means the letter for women is barred from the golf club word

parts.note: a wedge is a lofted golf club

explanation.surface: A golf club's men-only rule is cast as its competitive advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface mocks men-only golf clubhouses, but the club here is the iron called a WEDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the edge over a rival means having a slight advantage or lead.

clue.text: Could be barking in tea-garden

indicators.note: barking, as in barking mad, says the letters of tea-garden go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: A large dog may be heard barking in a garden where tea is served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' doubles as a big dog's noise and slang for mad, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Great Dane is a giant breed of dog, the kind of animal that might be heard woofing in a café garden.

clue.text: Heard what summer does for a cutter

indicators.note: Heard says the phrase is spoken aloud and we enter the word that sounds the same

parts.note: a summer is someone who sums, and what such a person does is add up figures

explanation.surface: A listener learns what the warm season does for a woodworker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is not the season but a person who sums, pronounced 'summer' all the same.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is an axe-like woodworking tool with an arched blade, used for shaping timber.

clue.text: David Ellis is jolly unwise

indicators.note: jolly suggests the letters of David Ellis are cheerfully shaken up

explanation.surface: A man named David Ellis is described as very foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' reads as the British intensifier 'very', but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-advised means unwise or imprudent, done without proper thought.

clue.text: Plan diluted by opponent of progress

indicators.note: to plan is to lay out or arrange, so the instruction is to arrange the letters of diluted anew

explanation.surface: A scheme is watered down by someone who resists progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plan' looks like a noun being diluted, but as a verb it orders the letters of DILUTED to be set out afresh.
explanation.definitionFit: The Luddites were machine-breaking textile workers, so the word now means someone who resists new technology.

clue.text: Service veteran cooked

parts.note: Mass is a church service
aged means old, like a veteran

explanation.surface: An old soldier from the armed services has prepared a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' means falsified, as in cooked books; 'Service' is a church service, not the military.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook figures is to fiddle them, and massaged figures have been manipulated to look better.

clue.text: One old coin of a region

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, meaning one
the real was an old silver coin of Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: Someone describes a single antique coin from a particular area.
explanation.definitionFit: Areal is the adjective of area, describing something relating to a region or territory.

clue.text: Capital permits? Number falling

indicators.note: falling means the letter for number drops away from the word for permits

parts.note: assents means agrees to or permits

explanation.surface: Building permits are issued for capital projects, but numbers are dropping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is N, which drops out of ASSENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's assets are its property and resources, effectively its capital.

clue.text: M east citizen troubled by us aid?

indicators.note: troubled indicates that the letters of us aid are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern citizen is upset by American aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'M east' is the Middle East; 'us' is read as the United States, though it is simple fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A Saudi is a native of Saudi Arabia, a Middle Eastern kingdom.

clue.text: Separation involving one with new residence?

indicators.note: new says the letters are made anew, rearranged into a fresh order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A separating couple, one of them having moved to a new home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal, though the surface reads it as a fresh home for one partner after a split. A decree nisi is the provisional court order in an English divorce.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree nisi is the provisional court order in an English divorce, the legal step towards a couple parting.

clue.text: Scoff at being behind fourth in st Leger

indicators.note: being behind means the word at comes after the picked letter
fourth in picks the fourth letter of the phrase st Leger

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a horse running fourth in a famous race.
explanation.walkthrough: The St Leger is a classic British horse race at Doncaster; 'Scoff' means eat greedily, not mock.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff food is British slang for gobbling it up greedily.

clue.text: Some without a house in state

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A homeless person is described as being in a certain state.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'in state' does not swap for a state's name; 'in' is a link, and 'state' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty United States, in the American West.

clue.text: Wine can get you real drunk in club before "time"

indicators.note: in puts the shuffled letters between the club and time letters
before places the club letter ahead of the time letter

parts.note: C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of real are staggering out of order

explanation.surface: Someone gets truly drunk on wine in a club before closing time is called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles the letters of 'real' to give LARE, which sits between the club and time letters; in the surface, 'time' is the barman's call for last orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine.

clue.text: Prompt row involving male? It goes on briefly in the morning

definitions.text: It goes on briefly in the morning

parts.note: to egg someone on is to prompt or urge them

indicators.note: involving means the word for row encloses the letter for male

parts.note: a tier is a row, as in tiers of seats

explanation.surface: A prompt row breaks out involving a man.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a kitchen device run for a few minutes at breakfast to time boiled eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sand-glass or kitchen device runs for a few minutes to time a boiled breakfast.
